subject: Privileged network model clarification — NAT/egress patterns & allowlist needs
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Murphy <alex.murphy@finledger.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap — deployment mode and VPC connectivity asks

Alex — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and the follow-up asks so we can size the Private VPC proposal correctly: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary preference: Private VPC (customer-managed VPC with PrivateLink back to Redwood) to satisfy data residency and audit controls.
- Secondary fallback: Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput if PrivateLink cannot be provisioned in time.
- Workload shape: bursty inference (short prompt, high qps spikes), KV cache recommended.

Network/egress questions (need answers to finalize engineering scope):
1) Which egress model do you want for outbound tokenization/callouts? Options:
   - Customer-managed NAT gateway (preferred for many enterprise customers)
   - Routed egress via a transit VPC / VPN tunnel back to your on-prem
   - Allow Redwood-managed egress IPs (we can provide static IPs)
2) If customer-managed NAT: what are the public IP ranges/allowlist we should expect?
3) PrivateLink vs VPC Peering: you mentioned PrivateLink could be faster for ops — can you confirm if your security team requires PrivateLink specifically?
4) Firewall/proxy in front of endpoints — will there be TLS inspection that we should be aware of?

Next steps I propose:
- You share the egress IP ranges and the CloudOps contact (we can kick off an engineering pairing call).
- Redwood to prepare a short preflight checklist and a tentative timeline for PrivateLink setup (attached: redwood-privatenet-checklist.pdf).
- If there are procurement constraints, loop in Procurement and we’ll surface the Dedicated capacity estimate as contingency.

Attachments: redwood-privatenet-checklist.pdf (preflight checklist)

Thanks — let us know if any of this is off. Happy to run a 30-min engineer-to-engineer session this week.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Alex Murphy <alex.murphy@finledger.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudOps Team <cloudops@finledger.com>, Procurement <procurement@finledger.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — deployment mode and VPC connectivity asks

Thanks, Sofia — this matches our notes. A few answers and clarifications below.

1) We do want PrivateLink if possible — security has a strong preference for interface endpoints rather than peering for audit and traffic separation.
2) Egress model: we want customer-managed NAT for outbound egress (so calls to other third-party APIs will originate from our egress IPs). Redwood providing static IPs is OK as fallback but not preferred.
3) Our CloudOps contact is cloudops@finledger.com (CC'd). They will provide the allowlist ranges — see their note below.
4) No TLS inspection at the perimeter for these connections; internal proxies are used but they terminate TLS.

We are targeting an internal decision by end of next week (7/30) so the M&A and security teams can review the proposed diagram.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Murphy
Head of Platform, FinLedger
alex.murphy@finledger.com | +1 (212) 555-1984

> We do want PrivateLink if possible — security has a strong preference for interface endpoints rather than peering for audit and traffic separation.

Sofia / Redwood — attaching our egress IP list and a simplified topology. For the customer-managed NAT approach the public IPv4s you should expect to see in our egress will be: 18.203.12.0/28, 18.203.12.16/28, 18.203.13.0/28. We can provide ASN and VPC IDs in the engineer pairing call.

Attachment: finledger-network-topology.png, finledger-egress-ips.csv

Notes:
- We'll create an IAM role for the PrivateLink handshake stage and short-lived creds for your infra engineer.
- Recommended timeline: pairing call this week, PrivateLink interface endpoint provisioning by our networking team within 5 business days after engineering alignment.

--

Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — deployment mode and VPC connectivity asks

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the egress ranges — helpful. A couple operational items from our side so we can align the Scoped Statement of Work and timeline: 

- Can CloudOps confirm the VPC ID and the account ID (for PrivateLink interface creation)? If you prefer, we can share a short secure form rather than email.
- We'll propose an engineer-on-engineer call (30 mins) Thursday 7/23 15:00 UTC — does that work for your networking lead?
- If PrivateLink proceeds, Redwood will ship an initial allowlist of the control-plane IPs we need (for health checks and model fetches). If customer-managed NAT is the path, we'll instead provide a small set of static egress IPs you can expect for outbound activity from our runtime.

Action items assigned:
- CloudOps: confirm VPC & account IDs + upload any firewall proxy details (deadline: 7/22 EOD).
- FinLedger Procurement: if procurement needs a quote for Dedicated capacity as contingency, we'll send pricing (Ben).
- Redwood (Ben/Sofia): schedule engineer pairing and share control-plane allowlist stub.

I'll attach the draft mutual action plan after this — linking in the HubSpot deal as well: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DL-2026-058
